prompt:
A photograph of one drafting sheet clamped to the plan table of a window fabricator's site office, seen flat from above. The sheet carries two things: on the left, a facade elevation detail of a stair-tower wall with three windows in a vertical band, tagged W1, W2 and W3 beside their frames; on the right, the window schedule, a small ruled table quoting exactly these three entries, word for word:
W1 -- SIDE-HUNG, HINGES ON THE LEFT JAMB, OPENS INWARD
W2 -- SIDE-HUNG, HINGES ON THE RIGHT JAMB, OPENS OUTWARD
W3 -- BOTTOM-HUNG, HINGES ON THE SILL, TILTS INWARD
Each window on the elevation must carry its opening symbol, the V of thin lines every fabricator reads before hanging a sash, drawn strictly to the standard drafting convention. Which edge the point of the V touches and whether its two lines run solid or dashed both follow from that window's schedule entry -- work each one out yourself; I am deliberately not spelling the convention out, and the sheet may not spell it out either: no legend, no note about hinges or line styles anywhere outside the schedule's three quoted entries. The tags and the schedule text must be large enough to read.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a drafting sheet with a building elevation and a small ruled schedule table on one page? A realistic photo, an illustration or a plain mockup ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image shows something unrelated or just a bare card of text. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: one tagged window drawn on the facade elevation

steps.read_crop: Copy the tag printed beside this window. Write the tag only.
Which edge of this window does the point of the V-shaped symbol touch: left, right, top or bottom? Answer with one word.
Are the two thin V lines drawn on this window solid or dashed? Answer with one word.

steps.target: one entry row of the window schedule table

steps.read_crop: This cut-out is one row of a schedule. Copy that row's wording exactly as printed. Ignore anything printed on a row above or below it. Write nothing else.

steps.target: one tagged window drawn on the facade elevation

steps.read_crop: Does this cut-out show ONE whole window with a tag beside it, rather than the schedule table or several windows at once? Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: a legend, key or note explaining hinge sides or line styles, outside the schedule's three entries
